candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene and standard precautions
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene with gloves
candidate.educational_objective: Apply CDC hand-hygiene requirements before and after glove use.

options.A: Gloves replace hand hygiene whenever intact gloves are worn.
options.B: Hand hygiene is unnecessary after glove removal if no visible contamination is present.
options.C: Hand hygiene before donning gloves is unnecessary whenever gloves are indicated.
options.D: When a task requires gloves, perform hand hygiene before donning them and always clean the hands after glove removal.

candidate.rationale: CDC states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. When a task requires gloves, hand hygiene should be performed before donning them and touching the patient or surroundings, and hands should always be cleaned after glove removal. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene; perform hand hygiene before donning gloves when the task requires them and always after glove removal.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
candidate.source_locator: Know when to wear (and change) gloves
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: Which statement about glove use and hand hygiene is correct?
